body_markdown:
Codev works with AI coding agents to build and publish web applications with managed backend services. Teams evaluating alternatives may want mobile app publishing, different development workflows, or more control over their infrastructure.[Floot](https://floot.com/) is one option, offering full-stack app building through supported AI assistants and managed infrastructure.


This guide compares seven Codev alternatives for non-technical founders, business owners, and development teams. With the broader no-code AI platform market[valued at $4.06 billion](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/no-code-ai-platform-market) in 2025, builders have several approaches to consider, from conversational development to cloud IDEs and managed backend platforms.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Build through your existing AI assistant** :[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) lets supported AI assistants create, edit, and publish applications while Floot manages the infrastructure. Available actions depend on the connected client's permissions.
- **Reduce backend configuration** : Floot's[managed infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) includes PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, email, and hosting without requiring users to assemble separate services.
- **Understand development and hosting costs** :[Floot pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) separates daily build actions, optional AI credits, and hosting allowances, helping teams understand which costs apply to their projects.
- **Publish beyond the browser** : Floot's[mobile app builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) package web applications for iOS and Android, with monthly build allowances across all three plans and separate developer-account requirements.
- **Retain ownership of your work** : Floot users own their code and data on every plan. Its[export options](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) include database downloads on all plans and full project ZIP exports on paid plans.


## **Understanding AI App Builders and Codev's Position**


AI app builders transform natural language descriptions into functional applications. Depending on the platform, they may provide code generation, database provisioning, authentication, hosting, and deployment. The main differences involve how users interact with the AI, which infrastructure services are managed, and how development and operational usage are billed.


Codev works with coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. Its platform provides managed backend services, including data storage, sign-in, secrets, and proxy routes. Codev offers a Free plan and a Pro plan costing $29 per month, billed monthly.


Several considerations may lead teams to evaluate alternatives:


- **Web publishing focus** : Codev's listed capabilities emphasize web application deployment and managed backend services rather than an included native iOS and Android app-building workflow.
- **Free-tier limitations** : The Free plan includes one owned app, with defined limits for source storage, site requests, backend records, and operations.
- **Backend usage allowances** : The Free and Pro plans have different limits for managed backend environments, stored records, operations, and data transfer.
- **Development workflow preferences** : Some builders prefer an integrated AI interface, while others want to use an existing assistant or coding environment.


These considerations make the underlying development model important. For example,[how Floot works](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) illustrates an approach in which an AI assistant handles development through a connector while the platform provides managed application infrastructure.


Teams comparing AI builders can also review Floot's[platform comparisons](https://floot.com/blog/best-lovable-alternatives-in-2026-apps-that-can-actually-ship) to understand differences in development workflows, infrastructure, and publishing options.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, test, and publish applications through supported AI assistants. It provides managed infrastructure while the connected AI assistant handles development actions.


Floot supports Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, along with other supported MCP clients. The building capabilities available through each client depend on its connector permissions and supported tools.


### **Primary Focus**


Floot helps non-technical founders, operators, and business owners build working applications with saved data, user accounts, and backend functionality without assembling their own infrastructure.


The platform supports three development workflows:


1. Build through Claude or compatible ChatGPT configurations using the Floot MCP connector.
2. Connect coding environments such as Codex and Cursor through supported MCP workflows.
3. Use Floot's optional in-app AI agent when a separate building interface is preferred.


These workflows make Floot suitable for users who want managed full-stack infrastructure alongside familiar AI development tools.


### **Key Capabilities for Full-Stack Development**


- **AI assistant integration** : The[MCP connection](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) allows supported assistants to work with Floot projects through the available connector tools.
- **Managed PostgreSQL** : Applications receive a managed database with table browsing, SQL queries, and database export capabilities.
- **Built-in authentication** : Email/password authentication and brokered Google and Microsoft sign-in help applications manage user accounts.
- **Mobile app conversion** : Floot packages existing web applications into iOS and Android app builds without requiring users to maintain separate native codebases.
- **Code ownership** : Users retain ownership of their application code, data, and intellectual property, with full project ZIP downloads available on paid plans.
- **Application hosting** : Floot provides managed hosting and live application URLs. Free accounts receive a one-time $3 hosting credit, while Pro and Power include monthly hosting allowances. Additional usage draws from prepaid hosting credit.


### **Production Infrastructure Included**


Floot provides managed services for applications that need more than a static interface:


- Serverless backend endpoints for application logic and APIs
- File storage for uploads and assets with CDN-backed delivery
- Email services and push notification support
- Scheduled tasks and background operations on paid plans
- Custom domain support on Pro and Power plans
- Payment integration for customer-facing applications, with live payment processing subject to plan requirements


Developers can also connect supported coding tools to Floot rather than replacing their existing workflow.


### **Pricing Structure**


According to[Floot's pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , the platform is free to start and offers three plans with different building-action limits, AI credits, hosting allowances, and mobile build allocations.


- **Free ($0/month)** : 100 building actions per day, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, a one-time $3 hosting credit at signup, and 2 mobile app builds per month.
- **Pro ($25/month)** : 1,000 building actions per day, 5,000 monthly AI credits, a $10 monthly hosting allowance, 12 mobile app builds per month, and custom domain support.
- **Power ($100/month)** : 5,000 building actions per day, 15,000 monthly AI credits, a $25 monthly hosting allowance, unlimited mobile app builds, and custom domain support.


These prices reflect monthly billing in US dollars. Annual billing provides two months free on the paid plans.


Building through a supported AI assistant uses the user's existing AI subscription or API arrangement rather than a separate Floot AI agent credit charge for ordinary connector-based development. Floot's daily building-action limits still apply, and generating images or using optional AI features may consume AI credits.


Hosting usage first draws from any applicable plan allowance, followed by the account's prepaid hosting balance. Free accounts have no recurring monthly hosting allowance. Automatic credit reloading is optional and disabled by default.


Floot also includes[mobile publishing workflows](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) . Connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan, and publishing applications to the App Store or Google Play requires the appropriate developer accounts. Store approval is not guaranteed.


Floot has a[4.8/5 G2 rating](https://www.g2.com/products/floot/reviews) , based on eight published reviews as of November 16, 2026. The company was also part of Y Combinator's Summer 2025 batch.


For founders who already use Claude or ChatGPT, Floot offers an approach that combines conversational development with managed infrastructure while keeping the AI subscription and Floot platform charges distinct.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is a browser-based AI app builder that generates applications from natural language prompts. It supports React-based development and includes visual editing capabilities for refining layouts without describing every change through text.


### **Primary Focus**


Lovable emphasizes app creation through its integrated AI interface. Its Visual Edits feature allows users to adjust layouts, spacing, and components within the preview.


The platform also supports GitHub synchronization, making it possible to work on generated code outside the browser-based building environment.


### **Key Features**


- **Visual editing** : Adjust layouts, spacing, and components through Visual Edits instead of describing every change through prompts.
- **Backend options** : Lovable Cloud provides managed authentication, database, storage, and backend functions, while Supabase is available as an integration.
- **GitHub synchronization** : Connect projects to GitHub repositories for code access and developer collaboration.
- **Browser-based development** : Build, preview, and refine applications inside the platform.
- **Managed publishing** : Deploy generated web applications through the supported hosting workflow.


### **Considerations for Teams**


Lovable uses a credit-based system for AI-assisted development. Teams using Claude or ChatGPT elsewhere should account for Lovable's separate AI usage and subscription costs.


The platform primarily focuses on web applications rather than providing a built-in native-shell mobile conversion workflow equivalent to Floot's.


Teams deciding between these approaches can review the[Floot vs Lovable](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-lovable-compare-ai-no-code-platforms-2025) comparison for more information about connector-based development, AI credits, and code ownership.


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new, developed by StackBlitz, uses WebContainer technology to run a Node.js development environment in the browser. It supports natural language application development, live previews, and multiple frontend frameworks.


### **Primary Focus**


Bolt.new combines AI app generation with browser-based development tools. Users can describe an application, generate its code, preview changes, and work with files and packages inside the development environment.


The platform supports several frameworks, including React, Vue, Svelte, and Astro.


### **Key Features**


- **WebContainer technology** : Run Node.js-based development workflows directly inside the browser.
- **Multi-framework support** : Generate applications using React, Vue, Svelte, Astro, and other supported frameworks.
- **Browser IDE** : Access project files, terminal tools, and package management.
- **Backend services** : Use supported database and hosting capabilities for full-stack applications.
- **Free-tier allocation** : The Free plan includes 1 million tokens per month, with a daily limit of 300,000 tokens.


### **Considerations for Teams**


Bolt.new uses token-based limits, so teams should monitor consumption during development and debugging. More complex changes may require additional iterations.


The platform is designed around its own development environment, which may suit teams that prefer browser-based application building.


Teams comparing the two approaches can read[Floot vs Bolt](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-bolt-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) for a closer look at managed infrastructure and development workflows.


## **4. Replit**


Replit provides a cloud development environment with an AI Agent that can generate, test, debug, and deploy applications. It serves both non-technical builders and developers who want access to coding tools alongside AI-assisted development.


### **Primary Focus**


Replit combines natural language app development with a cloud IDE. Users can build through conversational instructions while retaining access to project files, a terminal, package management, and deployment controls.


Its Agent can run tests, identify bugs, and attempt fixes autonomously. Replit has documented autonomous sessions lasting up to 200 minutes.


### **Key Features**


- **Cloud IDE** : Integrated code editor, terminal, package management, and collaboration features.
- **Self-testing Agent** : AI that can run tests, identify errors, and attempt corrections.
- **Extended autonomous sessions** : Support for longer development tasks with autonomous execution.
- **Native mobile development** : Build mobile applications using Expo and supported app store publishing workflows.
- **ChatGPT integration** : Create and update Replit projects through supported ChatGPT integrations.


### **Considerations for Teams**


Replit uses effort-based Agent pricing, meaning development costs can vary according to the complexity and duration of tasks.


Teams should monitor Agent usage during longer debugging cycles to manage credit consumption.


Its ChatGPT integration also uses Replit Agent credits. This differs from Floot's connector-based development, where the connected assistant performs the development work through Floot's infrastructure tools.


For a closer comparison, see[Floot vs Replit](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-replit-compare-ai-vibecoding-platforms-in-2026) .


## **5. v0 by Vercel**


v0 is an AI-powered application development platform with strong support for React and Next.js workflows. It supports full-stack application creation, visual editing, and deployment through the Vercel ecosystem.


### **Primary Focus**


v0 emphasizes code generation and application development using React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui components.


The platform includes Design Mode for visual editing and supports Figma-based workflows for interpreting design references and generating application code.


### **Key Features**


- **React and Next.js specialization** : Generate applications using the React ecosystem and related component libraries.
- **Figma support** : Use supported Figma connections, design files, and visual references to guide code generation.
- **Design Mode** : Adjust generated interfaces visually before applying changes to the code.
- **Vercel integration** : Deploy generated applications through Vercel's hosting infrastructure.
- **Full-stack support** : Build API routes, backend functionality, and database integrations through supported workflows.


### **Considerations for Teams**


v0 is especially relevant to teams working with React and Next.js. Other framework requirements may make a different development environment more appropriate.


Although users can start with natural language prompts, developers who want deeper customization can work directly with the generated code and associated services.


Teams seeking managed PostgreSQL, authentication, storage, and hosting without configuring separate services can also evaluate[Floot's infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) .


## **6. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets eligible users create, preview, publish, and share interactive websites and lightweight applications through ChatGPT. Users can describe what they want, refine the result conversationally, and publish a hosted site without arranging a separate deployment platform.


### **Primary Focus**


ChatGPT Sites focuses on creating hosted websites and lightweight applications directly within supported ChatGPT workflows.


It includes built-in hosting, access controls, storage, and database functionality. Supported applications can save user information, accept file uploads, and provide sign-in experiences.


### **Key Features**


- **ChatGPT-native building** : Create and edit websites or lightweight applications using natural language.
- **Built-in hosting** : Publish Sites with shareable URLs and configurable access settings.
- **Interactive applications** : Build dashboards, trackers, internal tools, and other experiences with supported storage and database functionality.
- **User access controls** : Configure sharing permissions and supported sign-in options.
- **Custom domains** : Connect an existing domain where the feature is available for the account.


### **Considerations for Teams**


ChatGPT Sites supports database-backed applications, but it operates within its supported hosting environment. Framework choices, backend technologies, background processing, and deployment requirements may differ from those of a dedicated full-stack app platform.


Availability also depends on the user's ChatGPT plan and workspace permissions.


Teams needing managed PostgreSQL, payments, email services, and native-shell mobile app builds can use[Floot through ChatGPT](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , provided their ChatGPT configuration permits the required connector operations.


## **7. Base44**


Base44 is an AI app-building platform that lets users create applications through natural language prompts. It provides managed backend functionality, including a database, authentication, hosting, and integrations.


### **Primary Focus**


Base44 combines conversational app generation with managed application infrastructure. Users describe the application they want, refine it through AI-assisted interactions, and publish it through the platform.


The platform also provides developer-oriented workflows that can connect coding agents and existing development environments to its backend services.


### **Key Features**


- **Natural language app building** : Generate and modify applications through an integrated AI interface.
- **Managed database** : Store and retrieve application data without manually provisioning a separate database service.
- **Authentication** : Add user registration, sign-in, and access management.
- **Backend functions** : Implement server-side logic and connect external services through supported functions and integrations.
- **Built-in hosting** : Publish applications through the platform's deployment workflow.
- **Developer workflows** : Use supported CLI and SDK tools to connect existing development environments.


### **Considerations for Teams**


Base44 provides both an integrated conversational builder and developer-oriented backend workflows. The available capabilities and usage allowances vary by plan.


Its AI-assisted building experience uses platform-defined credit and feature limits, so teams should review the cost of development activity separately from application hosting and operational requirements.


For a comparison of development models and infrastructure, see[Floot vs Base44](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-base44-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) .


## **How Can Floot Help You Build and Publish a Full-Stack App?**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) offers an alternative for founders and operators who want working applications without managing separate backend services. Its MCP connector lets supported AI assistants handle development while Floot provides the infrastructure needed to host and operate the application. Available connector actions depend on the permissions and capabilities of the AI client.


A typical Floot workflow includes:


- **Connect your assistant** : Follow the[connector setup](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) for Claude, Codex, Cursor, or a compatible ChatGPT configuration.
- **Describe the application** : Explain the pages, user accounts, saved data, and workflows you need.
- **Build and test** : Use supported development actions to create, modify, and test the application.
- **Publish your project** : Deploy the web application and use[mobile publishing](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) when iOS or Android builds are needed.


Floot is free to start, with paid plans providing higher daily action limits and hosting allowances. The[pricing page](https://floot.com/en/pricing) explains these allowances and additional usage costs, helping teams choose a plan that fits their development and publishing requirements.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What makes Floot different from Codev?**


Both Floot and Codev work with AI development tools and offer managed backend capabilities. Floot emphasizes full-stack app building through its MCP connector, along with managed PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, hosting, and mobile app workflows. The[Floot platform overview](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) explains how supported AI assistants handle development while Floot provides the infrastructure. Available actions depend on the connected client's permissions.


### **Can Floot build and publish iOS and Android apps?**


Yes. Floot can package web applications into iOS and Android builds. Its[mobile app documentation](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) explains the process and available build allowances. The Free plan includes 2 monthly builds, Pro includes 12, and Power includes unlimited builds. Apple and Google developer accounts are required for store publishing, and Google Play connection requires a paid Floot plan. Final approval depends on the app stores.


### **How does Floot's pricing compare with Codev?**


Codev's Pro plan costs $29 per month, while Floot's Pro plan costs $25 per month with monthly billing.[Floot's pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) includes 1,000 daily building actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, a $10 monthly hosting allowance, and 12 monthly mobile builds on Pro. Users building through the Floot connector pay separately for their existing AI subscription or API usage. Floot does not impose a second AI agent credit charge for ordinary connector-based building, although action limits, optional AI features, and hosting usage still apply.


### **Do I need coding experience to build with Floot?**


No coding experience is required to get started. Floot is designed for people who can describe the application they need but do not want to configure databases, authentication, or hosting themselves. Users can build through supported conversational workflows, including Claude and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Developers can also use Codex, Cursor, and other MCP clients. The[Floot connector guide](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) explains how supported assistants interact with projects and why available actions depend on client permissions.


### **Can I export my app's code and data from Floot?**


Yes. Floot states that users own their project code, application data, and intellectual property on every plan. Database exports are available on all plans, while downloading the complete project as a ZIP requires a paid plan. Floot's[code export documentation](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) explains the available options. Teams planning to self-host should also review the changes needed to replace Floot-managed services such as authentication, storage, and backend infrastructure.
